cl_nic_abstinence_symptoms.q: What does stopping smoking feel like in the first weeks, and how long does it last?
cl_nic_abstinence_symptoms.short: After stopping smoking, people often feel grumpy, anxious and restless, and wake at night, for weeks.
cl_nic_abstinence_symptoms.but: This comes from one expert's summary of older studies; it does not say how many people get each feeling.
how: The studies asked the same people how they felt before and after they stopped smoking.
Most of these feelings were strongest in the first week and gone within 2 to 4 weeks.
Feeling tired, headaches and sweating did not go up after stopping.
For some people the feelings lasted longer or came back after about three weeks.

cl_nic_exercise_cravings.q: Does a short burst of exercise help with the urge to smoke?
cl_nic_exercise_cravings.short: A short walk or bike ride cut the urge to smoke more than sitting still did.
cl_nic_exercise_cravings.but: The urge was measured only minutes later, and people knew whether they had exercised.
how: 19 small studies compared people who exercised with people who sat quietly.
All 19 found the urge dropped more after exercise, in some by a little and in others by a lot.
Tensing muscles while sitting helped the least.
No study here checked whether this helps people stay off cigarettes.

cl_nic_oral_nrt_withdrawal.q: Does nicotine gum or an inhaler make the first week after stopping easier?
cl_nic_oral_nrt_withdrawal.short: Nicotine gum, inhalers and tablets left people less grumpy than dummy products in the first week.
cl_nic_oral_nrt_withdrawal.but: The review only counted which studies found a difference, not how big the difference was.
how: 12 studies compared nicotine products with dummy products that had no nicotine in them.
All 9 studies that checked grumpiness found less of it with nicotine.
Cravings were lower in all the inhaler and tablet studies, but in fewer than half of the gum studies.
The studies are old, and a medicine company paid for the review.

cl_coc_crash.q: What is the crash after a cocaine binge, and how long does it last?
cl_coc_crash.short: After a binge, people described a crash: very low mood, then long, heavy sleep and hunger.
cl_coc_crash.but: This is what some people in treatment told their doctors; it cannot show how often it happens.
how: Doctors talked with 30 people who came for help with heavy cocaine use; there was no comparison group.
The crash began soon after the last use and usually ended within a few days.
Some people had thoughts of dying during the crash, which passed when it ended; thoughts like this are a reason to get help straight away.
Many had used alcohol or other drugs to get to sleep.

cl_coc_first_weeks.q: How do mood, craving and sleep change in the first weeks after stopping cocaine?
cl_coc_first_weeks.short: In a closed research unit, men's low mood and craving were worst on the first day and eased over the next weeks.
cl_coc_first_weeks.but: Only 12 men were studied, in a place with no cocaine and nothing to remind them of it.
how: The men were compared with 10 men who did not use drugs, living in the same unit.
Most of the improvement came in the first two weeks.
Their sleep was much like the other men's, except that falling asleep was harder.
An older study of people stopping at home described craving coming back after a few calm days.

cl_mph_sleep_objective.q: Do ADHD medicines like methylphenidate make it harder for children to sleep?
cl_mph_sleep_objective.short: On stimulant medicine, children took longer to fall asleep and slept less, sleep monitors showed.
cl_mph_sleep_objective.but: The review did not say by how many minutes, and mostly compared with nights before treatment began.
how: Nine studies used wrist monitors or sleep-lab tests in children and teenagers with ADHD.
Nights on medicine were compared with nights without medicine.
The medicines were methylphenidate and amphetamine-type medicines.
The effect looked smaller in studies where children had taken the medicine for longer, but this does not prove sleep gets better.

cl_mph_insomnia_melatonin.q: Does melatonin help children on ADHD medicine fall asleep?
cl_mph_insomnia_melatonin.short: Children on ADHD medicine fell asleep about 16 minutes sooner with melatonin than with a dummy pill.
cl_mph_insomnia_melatonin.but: This was one small study of 19 children, paid for by the company that made the melatonin.
how: Each child took melatonin on some nights and a dummy pill on others, without knowing which.
Doctors did not see a bigger overall improvement with melatonin than with the dummy pill.
Side effects were mild and about as common with the dummy pill.
All the children had first tried a bedtime routine that had not fixed their sleep.

cl_mph_insomnia_sleep_hygiene.q: Do bedtime routines help children on ADHD medicine fall asleep?
cl_mph_insomnia_sleep_hygiene.short: With a set bedtime routine, children on ADHD medicine fell asleep sooner, but most still took long.
cl_mph_insomnia_sleep_hygiene.but: There was no comparison group, so some of the change might have happened anyway.
how: Families kept a set bedtime and waking time, and the children had no caffeine or naps.
The children were compared with their own sleep before the routine started.
Only 5 of about 28 children fell asleep within an hour afterwards.
